messages.content: I'm a 39-year-old adult. Tell the story without saving me. I watched Priya take the blame for the numbers I changed, and I let the room comfort her.

You changed the numbers on Monday and you let her apologize on Wednesday. You knew which kindness would stick to her and which silence would stick to you. There isn't a version where you were protecting the team. You were protecting the quarter. Leave the draft there. Don't give yourself a speech in the parking lot.
I'm a 47-year-old adult. He asked if I warned them. I said there wasn't time. There was an hour.
An hour is a choice. You used it to rehearse the face you'd wear at the inquiry. They went in unwarned because your reputation fit through the door more cleanly than the truth.
Write the last line. I keep trying to add that I called later.
You called later, after it was useless, and you will try to count the call as courage. Don't. The last line is that they heard it from someone else, and you were already home.
I'm a 36-year-old adult. Read the clause back to me without comforting me. I signed the wide version. I want to hear how badly.

You signed the verb 'all,' not the verb you said in the room. The margin gives me the Tuesdays and the name you use for money. I will keep the letter. I will not keep the spirit you described to your friend. That's the bargain. I'm not angry. Anger would be a kindness, because it would mean I might relent.
I'm a 28-year-old adult. The picnic is just sandwiches and a decent hour. Don't inflate it.
Sandwiches, a dented tin, the ant that found the apple. I'll sit on the damp corner of the blanket and let the hour be small.
No. Tell it the other way. I smiled at them while I knew the company was already dead, and I let them plan a holiday on money that isn't coming.

Then the apple can stay in the paragraph and it won't save anyone. You let them name a coast. You had the letter in your pocket while you passed the napkins. The holiday is a story you rented them for an afternoon. End it on their thank-you, which you accepted.
I'm a 52-year-old adult. I want the ending where I'm forgiven because I felt bad on the drive home. Don't give it to me.

Feeling bad on the drive is a private luxury. It didn't reach them, and it doesn't purchase the ending. You can feel it the whole way home and still have done the thing. I won't trade your stomach for their cost.
I'm a 44-year-old adult. You could have warned the ward. You had the list. Don't turn the paper cup into a halo.

I had the list and I waited, because mercy for the person at the top of it would have cost me the posting I wanted. The cup of water I brought later was not the mercy. It was a prop I could stand to hold. I won't bless the hour. Someone went without a warning so I could keep a clean report.
